skill.name: revnu-landing-page-audit
skill.description: Audit one landing page for message match, clarity, proof, calls to action, friction, and mobile usability. Receive up to seven prioritized fixes, with optional copy rewrites and requested repository edits.
skill.summary: Review landing page conversion barriers with evidence, prioritized fixes, and clear measurement limits.
skill.author: revnu-app

security_audit.summary: All 39 static alerts are false positives involving Markdown, audit terminology, scoped page captures, or consent-gated public-site requests. Two semantic concerns remain: conflicting connected-service sharing instructions and missing origin restrictions for returned polling URLs. No evidence found of credential theft, screenshot uploads, or instructions to override the security review.

remediation.issue: The connected handoff includes audit context despite a rule limiting Revnu submissions to the public website.
remediation.suggestion: Reconcile the sharing rules and require explicit approval of the exact handoff fields before sending audit context or business information.

remediation.issue: The preview workflow follows a service-returned polling URL without stated destination validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and an explicit trusted-origin allowlist for polling URLs, validate redirects, and reject local or private-network destinations.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting External Data-Sharing Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The connected workflow proposes sending traffic promises, agreed fixes, and shipment details through ask_revnu. The final rule instead permits only the public website, creating an ambiguous disclosure boundary for potentially private business context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff template explicitly includes information beyond a public website, contradicting the final sharing rule. A handoff is offered, but field-specific disclosure consent is not defined.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Service-Returned Polling URL
semantic_findings.description: The preview instructions tell the agent to poll a returned URL without requiring a trusted origin or rejecting private-network destinations. A compromised response could direct requests outside the intended service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions directly delegate the polling destination to a response field without validation guidance. Exploitation depends on the response and host protections; no malicious destination is shown.

content.user_title: Audit Landing Pages for Conversion Barriers
content.value_statement: Visitors may leave when a landing page does not match the promise that brought them there. This skill compares that promise with page evidence and returns up to seven prioritized fixes.
actual_capabilities: Compare advertising, post, or search promises with the first landing page headline and offer.
Review clarity, supporting proof, calls to action, form friction, and mobile usability.
Check available speed evidence and test advertising click identifiers across redirects.
Return up to seven prioritized fixes with locations, evidence, proposed changes, and effort estimates.
Provide two or three requested copy alternatives using supported facts or visible placeholders.
Edit requested page components in the repository, then compare renders and run available project checks.
limitations: The audit cannot promise conversion gains or establish reliable small effects from limited traffic.
Visual checks require a browser or screenshots; a plain fetch may miss client-rendered content.
The workflow excludes SEO audits, standalone speed engineering, new-page construction, deployment, and live ad changes.
The core audit needs no Revnu account; optional paid-service workflows require consent and have unresolved sharing and polling safeguards.

use_cases.title: Review Paid Campaign Message Match
use_cases.description: Compare an ad promise with its destination page and prioritize mismatches that could prevent visitors from taking action.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Signup Page
use_cases.description: Review the first phone screen, supporting proof, and signup friction before requesting evidence-based headline and button alternatives.

use_cases.title: Implement Scoped Page Fixes
use_cases.description: Audit an existing route, apply requested component changes, and verify phone and desktop renders without deploying.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [page URL] for visitors who should [desired action]. Return prioritized fixes and identify checks you cannot complete.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with a page and conversion goal.

prompt_templates.title: Compare the Ad Promise
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [page URL] against this ad: [headline and body]. Compare the promise, first phone screen, proof, and CTA. Do not contact Revnu.
prompt_templates.scenario: Campaign review with known traffic context.

prompt_templates.title: Use Device-Level Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [page URL] using [traffic source] and [visits and conversions by device] for [date range]. Separate observed barriers from measurement uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evidence-based prioritization with recent performance data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Edit a Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [repository route] against [ad promise]. Implement the top two fixes, provide three headline options, and verify mobile and desktop. Do not deploy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced repository workflow with scoped implementation.

output_examples.input: Illustrative review: an ad promises free invoicing, but the page headline says only Business tools for modern teams.
output: Verdict: The first headline does not confirm the specific invoicing offer in the ad.
Priority fix: Replace the general headline with a supported invoicing statement. Effort: minutes.
Could not check: Mobile layout, traffic volume, and conversion events require additional evidence.
Receipt: Copy comparison only. Nothing changed or published.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: rewrite a signup button labeled Submit, where the next step starts a free trial without a card.
output: Option 1: Start free trial. This names the action and matches the confirmed next step.
Option 2: Try it free. This keeps the action brief while retaining the supported offer.
Measure completed trial signups before and after the change. No percentage lift can be forecast from the label alone.

best_practices: Provide the exact traffic promise, desired action, and recent visits and conversions for the same page and date range.
Use phone and desktop evidence, and separate measured findings from checks that tools or access cannot support.
Keep the audit local unless you explicitly approve external service use and the exact information to share.
anti_patterns: Requesting guaranteed conversion gains or treating low-volume changes as statistically reliable.
Inventing customer proof, unsupported claims, testimonials, or performance numbers for stronger copy.
Deploying changes, submitting real forms, or sending private audit context to external services without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Do I need a Revnu account?
faq.answer: No. The landing page audit works without an account. Optional ongoing Revnu services are paid and require your agreement.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a page URL or repository route and the desired visitor action. Ad copy and recent conversion numbers improve the review.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a conversion increase?
faq.answer: No. It prioritizes evidence-based changes but does not forecast lift. Reliable measurement depends on traffic volume and an appropriate comparison.

faq.question: Can it change my page code?
faq.answer: Yes, when requested and the page is in the repository. It follows existing conventions and verifies changes without deploying or merging.

faq.question: What happens if browser access is unavailable?
faq.answer: It can inspect source or fetched content. It marks unsupported visual checks as unavailable and avoids judging an empty client-rendered shell.

faq.question: Does the optional integration share audit information?
faq.answer: Preview requests send the public site after consent. Connected handoff instructions also include audit context, conflicting with the website-only rule; approve exact fields first.
